I read `regeneration.py`, `tempergraph.regenerations.json`, and the stamp and revision test lines. I did not read the full listed source set. I graded criteria 9–12 mainly from those files plus the gate findings, so confidence is moderate.

**First blocker (`--json`):** it is fixed in the tree I read. All three declared commands end in `--json` (`tempergraph.regenerations.json:6,17,28`). `findings_of` (`regeneration.py:243-247`) reads the report from `row["report"]`, and `_run_one` fills that from the command's whole output file (`:155`). `_reported` (`:220-231`) emits one finding per rung finding. Two tests guard this. `test_regeneration.py:311` asserts every declared `author verify` command ends in ` --json`. `test_regeneration.py:296` runs a command that prints the JSON report. I did not open the test body at `:296` beyond its setup lines.

**Second blocker (stamp):** it is only partly resolved.
- The assertion `stamp["outcome_revision"] == o["revision"]` is still removed. The test at `test_spec_budget_and_moved_ids.py:297-301` now carries the comment "the stamp's refresh belongs to the unit, row 3.5".
- `stamp.json:104` still says 24 while `outcome.json:3` says 25.
- The code report (line 33) says the removal was a default "owner decision" taken without confirmation.
- I could not confirm that no other check relies on a current stamp.

Criteria 16–21 and 23 apply only when a command fails at the gate. Every command passed, with all four reused, so they are N/A. Criteria 24–26 are N/A per their own check findings.
